public_rationale: Agents already taking over work provide substantial counterevidence to a blanket denial of agent capabilities. Anthropic reports internal team redeployment, and Klarna reports considerable customer-service workload automation. Neither establishes the broader replacement capability and scale referenced in the claim. The early-resolution rule is therefore unmet. The absence of demonstrated mass replacement cannot support 'never'.
limitations: A narrower reading about any replacement of white-collar work would materially change the assessment.
The strongest deployment evidence here comes from interested companies.
The March labor study predates the October company report and does not negate it.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The agents that Dario Amodei says will replace white-collar workers in the next few years will never exist.

statement.excerpt: I truly believe there are multiple reporters who feel genuine excitement when they write scary stories about how Dario Amodei says white collar workers will be fired in the next few years in favour of "agents" that will never exist.
statement.document_title: The Hater's Guide To The AI Bubble

from_speaker: white collar workers will be fired
our_interpretation: Assess the prediction about agents, excluding the speculation about reporters' private feelings.
The contextual target is autonomous systems capable of replacing white-collar workers on the broad scale attributed to Amodei, not every tool marketed as an agent.
Amodei's warning provides scope, but its numerical employment projection is not silently imposed as a precise threshold Zitron supplied.
'In the next few years' describes the warning being rejected. Zitron's own 'never' prediction has no deadline.
A narrower claim that no agent could ever replace any white-collar work would face substantially stronger counterevidence.
criteria.support_condition: A finite observation period cannot establish that such agents will never exist. Support would require a decisive demonstration that the specified capability is impossible.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence establishes autonomous agents performing complete white-collar roles reliably at broadly deployable scale, with substantial realized worker substitution rather than task assistance alone.

evidence.excerpt: AI could eliminate half of all entry level white collar jobs within five years.
evidence.explanation: This identifies the broad employment warning referenced by Zitron. It is contextual reporting, used because the original interview page was inaccessible, and is not evidence that replacement occurred.

evidence.excerpt: handed off their work to agents.
evidence.locator: Labor demand at the frontier, paragraph on internal reallocation
evidence.explanation: This is material evidence that agents took over actual work, rather than merely existing as product labels. Internal redeployment at one AI company does not independently establish broad white-collar replacement.

evidence.excerpt: no extension do we find clear impacts on exposed jobs.
evidence.locator: Footnote 8, robustness checks of unemployment results
evidence.explanation: The study reports no clear unemployment effect in its specified tests. That limited finding neither proves permanent impossibility nor rules out substitution at particular employers.

Klarna's workload-equivalence claim is counterevidence to an unrestricted claim that AI cannot replace any white-collar work. It does not document 700 actual firings or establish the broader capability and scale at issue.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent, dated evidence of agents reliably performing complete white-collar roles at broadly deployable scale, supported by attributable worker-substitution records.
